comment: Every table in the public schema, as the database actually holds them.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Three gates on this server read tables that have
never existed — user_permissions, company_members and user_profiles. Each
returned an error object that a catch swallowed or a `|| []` coerced away,
so they were invisible: one of them, rewardsAdmin, was the ENTIRE check on
ten routes and refused everybody for as long as it existed. A permanently
refused admin route looks exactly like a correctly guarded one.
tests/serverTablesExist.test.ts asserts that every table named in a
.from('…') call appears here. That is the check which would have found the
whole class the day the first one was written.
TO REGENERATE, when a migration adds or removes a table:
and paste the names below. Regenerating is meant to be deliberate: if a
test failure sends you here, first ask whether the table is missing from
this list or missing from the database. The second is the bug this exists
to catch, and adding a name to this file would hide it.
knownMissingComment: Tables the FRONT END queries that do not exist. Found 2026-11-17 by the
check this file was written for — the server came back clean, the browser
did not.
This is a ratchet, not an allowlist: the test refuses any NEW name, and
the rest are recorded so the gate is not broken while they are decided
on. Shortening this list is the only correct direction — and the test
also fails when a name here is no longer queried, so the list cannot
quietly outlive the problem.
WENT ON 2026-11-19, each with the answer it got:
user_profiles      REMOVED. userService.ts had zero importers. KV
user_activity_log  already holds user_profile:<email> rows.
user_companies     REMOVED. companyScope's two functions were never
called; AuthContext imports only its types. The real
company-access decision is CompanyContext's, which
calls an RPC that does not exist either — see D-2.
company_documents  REMOVED. getDocuments/saveDocument/deleteDocument,
all three uncalled, no screen offered the feature.
company_settings   REPOINTED, and it was the one that mattered. The
customer work-request form measured distance from a
business address it read from here, so the service-
area warning had NEVER been shown to anybody. It now
reads GET /public/service-area, off the companies
table the rest of the platform already uses.
security_audit_log BUILT. It was the only security control on the list.
STILL HERE, and why:
stakeholders       Three dashboards on /reports. The components are
stakeholder_*      intact but no longer mounted — <FeatureNotBuilt />
audit_logs         stands in, so an empty report can no longer be
notification_templates  mistaken for a quiet week.
portals            /portal-management, same treatment. Its delete button
used to report success against this absent table.
company_members    the same phantom the server read until 2026-11-17.
Each wants one of three answers, and nobody should guess which: build the
table, delete the feature, or point it at the server route that already
holds the data in KV. See docs/audit-2026-11/REMEDIATION_PLAN.md, batch 4.
